title: Comparator-based RC relaxation oscillator with process/temperature-compensated reference
topology: An astable relaxation oscillator built from a timing capacitor that is repeatedly charged and discharged by a fixed reference current between two comparator-set threshold voltages, with a pair of comparators (or one comparator plus digital toggle logic) monitoring the capacitor voltage and flipping the charge/discharge direction (or switching between two capacitors in a ping-pong arrangement) each time a threshold is crossed, generating a clock whose period is set by C * delta-V / I rather than by any resonant LC or crystal element. Unlike a ring oscillator, whose period depends on gate propagation delay (itself a strong function of supply voltage and process corner), the relaxation oscillator's period is set by an explicit RC (or C/I) time constant referenced to a bandgap-derived voltage and current, which is the basis for its process/temperature compensation.
spec_class: low-cost, moderate-accuracy clock source — an on-chip alternative to a crystal oscillator for applications that can tolerate percent-level frequency accuracy (after trim) and tens-to-hundreds-of-ppm/C temperature drift, in exchange for zero off-chip components and much lower area/cost than a crystal + oscillator-driver solution; commonly used for watchdog timers, low-power wake-up clocks, and reference clocks in systems that later PLL-multiply up from it

pdk_portability.notes: The relaxation-oscillator architecture and its compensation strategy are process-independent, but the achievable frequency accuracy and drift depend on sky130-specific comparator offset/propagation-delay characteristics (comparator delay directly adds timing error to each half-period, so it must be small and stable relative to the target period) and on sky130's poly/metal or MiM/MoM capacitor temperature/voltage coefficients for the timing capacitor, both of which must be re-characterized rather than assumed portable. The reference current/voltage generation typically reuses a bandgap-style reference (e.g. kb/entries/sky130-bandgap-reference.json), whose own PDK-portability notes apply here as well.

sizing_approach: Set the nominal period from the C*delta-V/I relation: pick a timing capacitor value large enough that comparator input capacitance and parasitic routing capacitance are a small fraction of it (so they do not shift the period unpredictably), then size the charge/discharge current and comparator threshold spacing (delta-V) to hit the target period at that capacitor value; both the reference current and the threshold voltages should derive from the same underlying bandgap-style voltage/current reference so that first-order supply and temperature variation cancel in the C*delta-V/I ratio (as long as I and delta-V are both derived from the same reference with matched, opposite-signed sensitivities, the reference's own residual temperature coefficient becomes the oscillator's dominant drift term rather than the raw RC or C/I time constant, which is the compensation mechanism explored in the cited work). Size the comparators for propagation delay well below the target half-period (a good rule of thumb is under ~1% of the period) since comparator delay adds directly to each phase and, if delay itself varies with temperature/corner more than the RC term does, becomes the limiting error source; where higher accuracy is needed, budget for a one-time digital trim (adjusting the reference current, capacitor bank, or delay-compensation term) to remove residual process spread, since untrimmed relaxation oscillators typically show several-percent unit-to-unit frequency spread even with a compensated reference.
layout_idioms: timing capacitor implemented as a matched array of unit capacitors (MiM/MoM) rather than a single large device, both for better absolute-value matching to the reference-derived current and to support a trim/calibration bank
comparator input pairs placed with common-centroid/symmetric layout to minimize threshold-crossing offset, since comparator offset directly adds jitter and period error each cycle

charge/discharge current-source transistors laid out adjacent to and matched in orientation with the bandgap/reference current-mirror devices they derive from, to preserve the reference's temperature-coefficient cancellation through to the oscillator core

guard ring and physical separation between the oscillator core and digital switching logic (including any downstream clock buffers/dividers) to keep substrate and supply noise from perturbing the comparator threshold-crossing instants (a major jitter source in relaxation oscillators, unlike the resonant-element-dominated jitter of a crystal oscillator)

source.citation: K. Sundaresan, P. E. Allen, and F. Ayazi, "Process and temperature compensation in a 7-MHz CMOS clock oscillator," IEEE Journal of Solid-State Circuits, vol. 41, no. 2, pp. 433-442, Feb. 2006.
source.license_or_openness: Peer-reviewed IEEE journal paper cited here for its comparator-based RC relaxation-oscillator topology and process/temperature-compensation methodology only (no figures or text reproduced), per the KB's open-sources sourcing rule. This is a widely cited reference for deriving both the oscillator's timing current and its comparator thresholds from a single compensated reference to cancel first-order supply/temperature sensitivity in the resulting C*delta-V/I period.

notes: Positioned here as the low-cost end of the on-chip clock-source spectrum: pair it with kb/entries/sky130-bandgap-reference.json (or a lighter-weight reference such as kb/entries/cmos-subthreshold-voltage-reference.json where die area/current is more constrained than accuracy) for the current/voltage reference feeding the timing branch. Expect single-digit-to-low-tens-of-percent uncalibrated frequency spread and, after a one-time trim, drift dominated by the underlying reference's residual temperature coefficient plus comparator-delay variation -- meaningfully worse absolute accuracy than a crystal but sufficient for watchdog/wake-up timing and as a PLL reference where the PLL's own loop bandwidth and multiplication factor set the final accuracy requirement.

artifacts.notes: Behavioral (PDK-model-free) realisation of this topology, runnable headlessly via the request that wraps it: `klt sim examples/kb/rc-relaxation-oscillator/request.json`. It sweeps 3 process x 2 supply x 3 temperature corners and measures the oscillation period against limits. The charge current and the comparator thresholds both derive from one reference node, so the measured period follows the C*dV/I relation in sizing_approach rather than the supply -- but the behavioral comparator has no device-level delay or offset, so the netlist demonstrates the timing relation, not silicon accuracy.
